evidence: All 3D views show the ESP32 module, both tactile switches, USB-C, pin header and passives as separate bodies with clear gaps and no intersections or stacking.
In 3d_iso and 3d_iso_back every body sits flush on the PCB surface with no floating, sunken, or tilted parts.
In 3d_top each body is centered over its own footprint pads, including the ESP32 module aligned to its castellated pad ring and the switch bodies centered between their four corner pads.

USB-C J1 sits at the bottom-left edge opening outward, J2 is a vertical-entry pin header that does not require edge access, there are no relays, and the single polarized part D1 shows no inconsistent orientation.
The dashed antenna keepout runs along the top board edge ahead of the ESP32 module's antenna end and contains no components, pads, or visible copper in the 2D and 3d_top views.

In the 2D view C2 is stranded alone mid-board far from U1, R3/R4 float between the MCU and SW2 rather than sitting with either group, the switch-resistor pairs are not grid-aligned, and the large empty right/bottom regions make the layout read as scattered rather than tight clusters.
